Figure 3: Image translation from English to : a) Spanish (image source: Andre Carrotflower, CC BY-SA 4.0) , b) Chinese (photo captured by authors), and c) Japanese (image source: Drumguy8800, CC BY-SA 3.0)

Figure 6: OCR of handwritten French text under challenging conditions, including distortion, variable formatting, and complex image backgrounds: LLaMA3-MM OCR-SFT correctly identified three items with two accurate prices, while Gemini identified 4 items but produced one accurate price extraction. GPT recovered two accurate item names and one correct price (photo captured by authors).

Figure 1: Model architecture: image features are embedded and aligned with text tokens as inputs to the LLaMA decoder for multimodal generation. During training, the LLaMA and Perceiver module weights are updated through backpropagation, while the ViT encoder remains frozen. Our framework does not rely on an external OCR model.

Figure 4: Qualitative comparison between the baseline multimodal model (LLaMA3-VLM) and the OCR-augmented model (LLaMA3-VLM-OCR-SFT) on multilingual OCR translation tasks. Under both sparse and dense OCR conditions, the OCR-augmented model extracts substantially richer textual content and produces more complete French and German translations, demonstrating improved OCR grounding and robustness to complex visual text layouts (left photo generated by AI, right one is a brochure of the Outlet Shoppes at Atlanta)

Figure 5: a) OCR extraction in scenes containing multiple contextual visual elements. The OCRaugmented model recovers substantially richer receipt information, including purchase items, prices, timestamps, and seller details. b) Context-aware visual question answering with OCR reasoning under weak and partially visible text conditions (photos captured by authors).
